reviews.text: This doctor is a veterinarian I deeply respect, someone who cherishes each and every life and treats animals with the utmost care.

The issue of AERA featuring Professor Ota's interview is available.

A foster care event is scheduled to be held at the hospital on Sunday, November 12th at 2 PM. Those interested in fostering a cat are encouraged to attend. It seems that calico cats will be the main focus.

There are rumors that the hospital will be relocating near Shin-Koenji Station on the Marunouchi Line in the spring of 2027. This is hearsay.

Instead of solving everything with medication and surgery, this doctor prioritizes the owner's feelings for their pet and proposes a compassionate treatment plan. He's a man of few words, but truly has a deep love for living creatures. He'll refer you to a specialist if necessary, but I chose this doctor who made my pet feel safe and comfortable until the very end. Thank you so much.

I've been seeing this doctor occasionally for the past 10 years without realizing he's famous. He's a sincere doctor who treats mixed breeds and former rescue dogs with the same respect. I was hesitant to bring in my dog, who has a biting habit, but when the doctor asked him, "Does this dog bite?", he calmed down. I also took him in for an examination because I couldn't figure out the cause of his poor health and bad mood. I'm grateful that he found a tumor that had been overlooked elsewhere.

People have different feelings about veterinary consultations, and I understand there are many different opinions.

However, what I feel when I observe this doctor is that he always focuses solely on the animal in front of him and treats them with utmost sincerity. He carefully explains the condition and treatment plan to the owner, but he doesn't say things that sound good just to gain popularity; he prioritizes the treatment that is truly necessary for that animal.

Animals sometimes resist treatment, and symptoms don't always improve immediately. Even so, he never compromises on necessary procedures and treatments, and I always feel a sense of trust in his dedication to each and every animal.

I believe that compatibility with veterinarians is important, and it's also crucial to seek a second opinion when necessary. However, I feel that it's rare to find a doctor who puts animals first and treats them with such sincerity. He is a doctor I can confidently entrust my beloved family member to.
The same heartworm medication cost about twice as much at this nearby animal hospital.

In short, I feel that Dr. Ota truly considers things from the animal's perspective, taking into account the animal's condition and the energy and feelings the animal is conveying to him, and then proposes the best course of action. I am extremely grateful, and I appreciate that he is such a rare type of doctor. I have hearing difficulties, so sometimes I can't hear what he's saying and have to ask him to repeat himself many times, but regarding treatment, he is a doctor (hospital) I can truly trust. Thank you, Dr. Ota, Dr. Sonoyama, and all the nurses.

* Anal sac apocrine gland carcinoma removal surgery
* Cushing's syndrome medication treatment
* Liver disease, etc.

I was fortunate enough to adopt a rescue dog.

I am truly grateful, because without the veterinarian and nurses, this life might not have been saved.

I think it's amazing that they provide initial medical care, feeding, and other services as volunteers alongside their regular hospital visits.

I am deeply grateful for their kind words and have great respect for this hospital.

As the veterinarian wrote in their book, I believe dogs live on love.

I will continue to cherish my precious dog.

She has grown into a plump beauty.
When it comes to treatment, what the young person at the reception desk says and what the doctor says are different, so you need to be careful as this can cause a lot of loss.

This vet is terrible. My cat had a bad cough, so I gave her Depo-Medrol, a stronger steroid injection than usual. After that, she had trouble breathing, so I took an X-ray and he said her lungs were completely black instead of white, and that there was no fluid buildup so it wasn't pneumonia. Ridiculously, he said it might be muscle pain from her struggling and twisting her neck while getting her claws trimmed. I asked the vet if it was because of the Depo-Medrol, but he insisted it was the same as before, and I also mentioned that her gait was strange, but he seemed to dismiss it. Her symptoms gradually worsened, her breathing became more difficult, she couldn't jump anymore, she couldn't even lick a single Churu treat, and she couldn't put any weight on her legs when she went to the toilet, so it was practically just a continuous stream of urine. I got the X-ray showing her lungs completely black and got a second opinion, and it turned out that she had developed severe diabetes as a side effect of Depo-Medrol, her blood sugar levels were over 600, and peripheral nerve damage likely caused by diabetes, so she couldn't put weight on her hind legs and was constantly urinating. It was truly heartbreaking to watch. Her lungs were white, a severe case of pneumonia; she was really close to being killed. I don't think this doctor has any real knowledge or expertise in treating animals. What he says and does is utterly insulting, and I can't forgive him for threatening my beloved cat's life. He's been featured in the media and has a good image, but to put it bluntly, he's a quack! He should be known as a specialist in spaying and neutering rescue cats and dogs. Anything else he does will ruin lives that could have been saved! I wonder how many lives were lost because people trusted this doctor and went there. It's truly terrifying.

This doctor truly loves animals from the bottom of his heart and seems like someone who was born to serve them. Thank you so much to the doctor and the veterinary nurses for always staying late. I can't express my gratitude enough.

Thank you so much for your help with the surgery to remove the apocrine gland carcinoma from my dog's anus. My dog ​​is a senior at 14 years old, and I had almost given up hope, but your words, "This dog is still young," gave me the courage to go ahead with the surgery, and I'm so glad I did. If the cancer hadn't been removed, I can only imagine what kind of life my dog ​​would be living now, and it would have been heartbreaking. I will continue to rely on your care for his Cushing's syndrome medication. I also ask for your continued support for my other five dogs. I deeply admire your dedication, Doctor. Please take care of your own health as well.

After moving to the area, I was recommended to go to this vet from a friend and saw that the doctor had great reviews. We made an appointment for my cat’s annual checkup, but when we arrived on time, the (very small) reception area was packed with people already waiting. After waiting for over 20 minutes without hearing from the receptionist (and seeing that only 1 of the people who arrived before us had been called by the doctor in that time) we asked the receptionist how long it would take. She said “Well, 3-4 people are still ahead of you, so at least 30 minutes,” with no apology or anything.

Our cat gets very stressed at the vet, so we left and will be going to our old veterinarian. Waiting an hour after our scheduled appointment time to be seen by the doctor is ridiculous, especially with no apology or kind words from the staff. When we told them to cancel our appointment, as an extra 30 minutes was too long, she just said “okay.” This is the third veterinarian I have been to in Japan, and I have never experienced this before.

The doctor is apparently great, but if you value timeliness and kind staff, go somewhere better. I’m glad it was just an annual checkup and nothing was wrong with my cat, because that would have been extremely stressful. What’s the point of allowing people to schedule appointments if you don’t follow the schedule? Just bad business.
For difficult cases, it's safer to go to another hospital.

The hospital he originally went to said they couldn't treat him and that he wouldn't live long if his condition continued to worsen.
So we took him to Hana Animal Hospital for a second opinion, where he underwent surgery.
The enlarged tumor has shrunk, and he's now healthy again.

The doctor is someone who uses all of his knowledge and experience to save the life in front of him.
Of course, there are times when things don't go as expected. There are some harsh reviews, but I believe the number of lives he saves outweighs the number he doesn't save.
If you're unsure, it's best to take him for a second opinion. Or, it's a good idea to ask the doctor questions until you're satisfied.
In our household, we try to get opinions from doctors other than our trusted ones as well.

I'm not a "follower" of the doctor, but I'm truly grateful.
I came all the way from afar, but I'm really glad I came.

This is a story about something so careless that it really pissed me off. My cat occasionally gets severe eye irritation, so I regularly use "Senju Pharmaceutical One Clean for Animals 15mL," but I was running low and tried to buy it online. It's sold for around 590 yen, or up to 803 yen at the suggested retail price, but I felt safer buying it at the vet, so I inquired and they agreed to order it for me.

When I went to pick it up later, I was given "Pranoprafen eye drops," as stated on the prescription. It cost 1600 yen. After researching this medication, I found it contains steroids, which is different from what I ordered, and I don't want my cat to use such a strong drug. When I explained this to the receptionist, she seemed annoyed, went to the back, and brought out the One Clean I had ordered.

Without changing the prescription, she handed me the same prescription with "Pranoprafen eye drops" written on it, saying, "The price is the same, so just take it." This is completely unacceptable and wrong. The fact that something that normally costs 803 yen was being sold for 1600 yen is ridiculous, and I thought their practices were incredibly sloppy, so I mentioned it. The doctor came out and said something like, "The price goes up when we order it," but if that's the case, then they should have sold me the medicine they mistakenly gave me for 3000 yen, double the original price of 1600 yen. Their words and actions are completely contradictory.

I don't think it used to be like this, and I'm extremely dissatisfied and have lost a lot of trust. Hospitals aren't charities; they're businesses, but I wonder if this kind of business practice is acceptable.

I was so angry I almost wanted to lash out. I run a business myself, but the attitude of that receptionist was really bad—she acted like it was none of her business—and I understand why other people are writing negative comments.

Trust in places like this can crumble in an instant.
